correctness.rationale: The continuous unordered two-point space is modeled by disjoint-closure cubical cells: the Prue–Scrimshaw bounds for two points are one edge between essential vertices and three edges around an essential loop, valid for the simple wheel. Its inclusion is equivariant, so the homology isomorphism is equivariant regardless of the retraction used. For the quotient conclusion one can make a two-particle equivariant strong retraction explicitly: in a common edge order the coordinates x<y and interpolate to (0,1); in two adjacent edges with coordinates x,y measured from the common vertex interpolate to (x,y)/max(x,y); on disjoint closed edges keep configurations fixed. These formulas respect edge reversals, particle exchange and overlaps (when one particle is on the common vertex, push the other to its far endpoint; when max=1 the relevant configurations are fixed). They therefore glue and pass to both quotients. The cubical 1-skeleton is the connected two-token graph; the cell counts give Euler characteristic −n. For the top boundary, normalize every square in the e-fiber using e as its first oriented factor (with coefficient negated when this requires switching). The coefficient sum at the one-cells (e,v) is then the boundary on the vertex-deleted graph up to a single overall sign. The spoke fibers live on paths, killing their square coefficients, and the remaining rim-only fibers also live on paths. This resolves the proof's implicit orientation normalization and forces injectivity. Orient fixed edge factors and multiply by minus one when they are exchanged. Nontrivial rotations have no fixed cells unless a half-turn, for which the n/2 paired vertices and n/2 negative swaps cancel. For reflections, fixed spoke and rim factors or disjoint swapped rim pairs give the stated signed table; in the even vertex-axis case two swaps at fixed vertices are not disjoint, while in the even edge-axis case the two fixed reversed rim edges form one positive square. H_0 is trivial as a representation, so Hopf trace gives 1−T_0+T_1−T_2 and exactly the reflection-sign twist of the rim-edge module plus a line. The constant rim-edge vector and extra line survive rotations and both change sign under reflections. Subdivide the finite cubical complex equivariantly and average rational chains for the orbit homology.
